account:
Today I have had a vague feeling that town business might be happening without me, but I have not found evidence of a concealed gathering or scheme. At tea, my neighbour said the baker had described the bakery lanterns as welcoming lights, not something for a special occasion. When I asked specifically, the neighbour knew of no gathering. The baker later reported steady business—thirty loaves sold by late afternoon—and no new riverside news, and offered to supply bread for town-hall meetings. That offer is not evidence that any meeting is planned.

Freight has been advertising ferry crossings and deliveries from the ferry or east-landing warehouse, according to my neighbour. I heard some distant speech and shouting but could not make out its words, so I cannot say more about its purpose. It may simply be ordinary trade.

Builder is inspecting the roads and bridge. I authorized a visual bridge inspection, with two emeralds payable when the written report is delivered tomorrow at noon; I authorized no repairs or inn inspection. The neighbour saw builder inspecting but personally saw no hazards. There appears to have been some uncertainty involving the innkeeper about an inn inspection: the secretary explicitly could not confirm one. I should clarify any remaining misunderstanding rather than assume wrongdoing.

The secretary reported no new correspondence or receipts and expenses, and requested a book to record the bridge authorization. I gave one emerald for it. My subsequent spoken instructions were not heard, so I should verify the written terms tomorrow. I returned late for the afternoon office appointment, but am now home for nineteen o'clock. Tomorrow I should read the appointment book in the morning, keep the mill grain-inspection appointment, and receive the bridge report at noon. For now, the lanterns and ferry announcements have plausible ordinary purposes; my suspicion remains unconfirmed.
